content.rationale: the renderer and the static visual grammar of the interactive HTML page: the drawing of the graph is a renderer kept for the life of the canvas (tnturzro), which carries the element it drew for every node and every edge, the heights it has already measured for those boxes and one static set of arrowheads from one draw to the next, so a draw writes only the boxes and routes its layout changed instead of rebuilding the layers, the label heights are measured on the first draw of a graph revision and reused by every later draw, a one-node move measures only the box it moved and updates that node and its incident edges in the elements they already occupy and measures no box it did not move, and a height the move measures different from the one drawn before, when it changes the row the moved box sits in, moves the layers below that row by the difference through a single translation of their container rather than by repositioning, remeasuring or laying out their boxes one by one; the module turns the layout's geometry into the drawing the visual-spec records fix, a box for a decision, a rounded box for an evaluation, solid and dashed edges with a single arrowhead at the child end, and an unresolved edge visibly marked; and the stylesheet carries those fixed values as the static visual grammar of the page regions and of the graph, and now carries the appearance of the detail panel's entries as well — the listed id and the ref-path entry, the things this decision once excluded from its subject, and the amendment that replaces that exclusion. The appearance of the listed id is stated where that entry is selected: the entry rules of the stylesheet select the two class names the panel and the stylesheet share, and no third name — the id that names a node carries "detail__entry" as one class and the id that names no node carries "detail__entry--inert" as one class in full (sqwusxql) — so the class an entry carries is what decides which of the rules reach it. On the followable entry the stylesheet spends the link colour role the graph already draws its links in (tvoouwkn, oqotyplt), shows the pointer cursor (rqrlnzny), underlines the id's characters while the pointer rests over it (qnmuwwvw), and outlines the entry in the accent focus role while it has the focus (vvzptxmz, qqmrtwor); on the entry that names no node it spends the muted secondary role (mplxzxnm, mnwxnyks) and draws none of those three cues, and nothing in their place (kpkstnps) — the two rules being the whole of what this decision states about that entry, each aspect remaining what its own record settled. The appearance of the ref-path entry is stated the same way, on the one name the vocabulary adds for it: the entry rules of the stylesheet select "detail__ref" as that entry's whole class, one name in full, neither of the listed entry's two and nothing spelled out of them (ppkkmxxu, sqwusxql), so the path entry squvoxyr presents as a visible link is reached by the rules written against its own name and by no other name. On that entry the stylesheet spends the same link colour role the graph already draws its links in (xntonlmp, oqotyplt), shows the pointer cursor (plkskmxu), underlines the path's characters while the pointer rests over it (slksrtvm), and outlines the entry in the accent focus role while it has the focus (oolrzkvl, qqmrtwor) — the resting rule and the two state rules being the whole of what this decision states about that entry, each aspect again remaining what its own record settled, and neither entry's rules composed with the other entry's name. The grammar is thus still one static set of rules over the panel and the canvas: an entry's appearance is a rule on the class an entry of that kind carries, not a behaviour, a text, a mark of the panel's own or a cue invented here. The page shell, the entry point, the composition of the interactions, the markup element that emits the classes, the rest of the panel's presentation and the toolbar are not this decision's subject.
